sections.h2: What does the Shelby County judge of probate do when a house is sold?
sections.html:
The judge of probate is the county officer who takes a signed deed into the public record and collects the state's recordation tax on it. Alabama's section 40-22-1 says a deed or similar instrument cannot be received for record until the privilege tax is paid.

The Department of Revenue tells new owners to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office, bringing the deed along. For a Shelby County sale, that means two stops after closing: probate for the record, then the property tax office for the assessment.

We could not open the Shelby County government pages for the probate fee schedule, hours or e-recording rules, so none of those are listed here. Call the office or read its current fee sheet before you plan a closing date.

sections.h2: How is the deed tax figured on a Shelby County deed?
sections.html:
The tax is 50 cents for every $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, and it is figured on the actual price paid. Under section 40-22-1(c), only the value above a mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax is taxable.

The deed must arrive with proof of the real price, on a form the Department of Revenue develops, and the person signing attests that it is accurate in good faith. If no proof is given, the judge of probate bases the tax on the latest assessed value and adds a penalty. The statute sets that penalty at $100 or 25 percent of the tax actually due, whichever is greater, for someone who intentionally withholds proof after being asked.

ItemWhat section 40-22-1 says
Rate$0.50 per $500 of value or fraction
Tax baseActual price, less mortgage or lien that paid mortgage tax
Split of the taxTwo thirds to the state, one third to the county
Penalty for withheld proof$100 or 25 percent of tax due, whichever is greater
No tax requiredNominal-consideration title-perfecting deeds, corrected deeds, mortgage transfers that already paid

sections.h2: Which deeds are exempt, and what happens to a deed that spans two counties?
sections.html:
Several instruments carry no recordation tax. The statute lists deeds written for nominal consideration to perfect title, the re-recording of corrected instruments, and transfers of mortgages on which the mortgage tax was paid. When a deed is exempt, the judge of probate stamps it "No Tax Collected."

A deed covering land in two or more counties follows a separate route. The probate judge certifies the instrument to the Department of Revenue, which sets the value in each county. The filer can deposit an estimated amount to get the deed recorded right away, and any excess is refunded once the value is fixed.

That rule matters in Shelby County because several places straddle county lines. Vestavia Hills, Hoover, Helena, Leeds and Calera are each partly in another county, per the county's Wikipedia entry. A title company will check whether your parcel sits entirely inside one county.

sections.h2: Where is Shelby County and how big is it?
sections.html:
Shelby County sits in central Alabama, and its county seat is Columbiana. Wikipedia's county entry gives a total area of 810 square miles, 785 of them land, and names Alabaster as the largest city.

The county was established on February 7, 1818, and named for Isaac Shelby. The first seat was Shelbyville, in what is now Pelham. The seat moved to Columbia, now Columbiana, in 1826, and the current limestone courthouse was built from 1905 to 1906. The 1854 brick courthouse is now the Shelby County Museum and Archives.

Shelby County borders six other counties:

  • St. Clair County to the northeast
  • Talladega County to the east
  • Coosa County to the southeast
  • Chilton County to the south
  • Bibb County to the southwest
  • Jefferson County to the northwest

sections.h2: How fast has Shelby County grown?
sections.html:
Shelby County's population grew from 66,298 in 1980 to 223,024 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 238,552. For the 2020 census the county had 84,241 households and 89,060 housing units, and 78.1 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.

Growth followed the roads. Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 link the county to Jefferson County, and Wikipedia ties suburban growth in Pelham, Helena, Alabaster and Chelsea to that access. Other major routes are U.S. 231, U.S. 280 and several state roads.

The county's economy was farm-based for a long time. Wikipedia says soybeans have passed cotton as the main crop since about 1990, and that the county once hosted an early inland waterway on the Coosa River and an early east-west railroad. The county page lists CSX, Norfolk Southern and the Calera and Shelby Railroad among its railroads.

For a seller, the practical advice is to bring a signed deed, a correct legal description and a completed value form, because a deed that needs corrections costs time at the counter.

sections.h2: What land and schools define Shelby County?
sections.html:
The county is partly hilly and partly flat. Oak Mountain and Double Oak Mountain are the southern tail of the Appalachians, while much of the rest is farmland and pasture with lowlands along two rivers. The Cahaba River runs along the northern edge and the Coosa River valley takes in the east. Lay Lake is a large reservoir that borders Shelby and three other counties.

Schools are split among several systems. Shelby County Schools serves areas outside Hoover, Alabaster and Pelham, while Alabaster City Schools, Pelham City Schools and Hoover City Schools serve their own cities. Higher education includes the University of Montevallo and a Jefferson State Community College campus.

If you own property near a lake, river or the Cahaba, ask your insurer and the county about flood maps before you list. We did not find county flood zone figures on a page we could open, so none are given here.

sections.h2: What do Shelby County sellers run into at the probate office?
sections.html:
The common snags are about the paper, not the house. Watch for these:

  • A deed that names the wrong legal description or a misspelled owner, which may need a corrected deed.
  • No proof of the purchase price, which triggers the value penalty.
  • An unpaid property tax bill, since Alabama taxes turn delinquent after December 31.
  • An owner who has died, where the estate may need a court order before the house can be conveyed.

Alabama counties are not required to mail tax notices, so an owner who never received a bill is still responsible. A buyer should check payment status with the county before the deed is recorded.

Cash buyers pay the same tax and the same recording costs as anyone else. What a cash sale changes is the repair list and the wait for a buyer's lender, not the recording steps.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Shelby County, Alabama?
faqs.a: The judge of probate. The Alabama Department of Revenue tells buyers to record the deed in the probate office and then assess the property at the county revenue office.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama deed tax rate?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, under section 40-22-1, less any mortgage or lien that already paid mortgage tax. Two thirds goes to the state and one third to the county.

faqs.q: Do I need to show the sale price when I record a Shelby County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, using a Department of Revenue form. Intentionally withholding it after a request carries a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax, whichever is greater.

faqs.q: Is any deed recorded without tax?
faqs.a: Some are. Deeds for nominal consideration that perfect title, corrected deeds and mortgage transfers that already paid tax are listed as exceptions, and the probate judge stamps them "No Tax Collected."

faqs.q: What are the recording fees in Shelby County?
faqs.a: We could not open the county's fee schedule, so we are not quoting a number. Ask the Shelby County probate office for the current schedule before closing.
